newsitem.title: CANADA: KLM to suspend Calgary flights.
newsitem.headline: KLM to suspend Calgary flights.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV said on Thursday it will suspend its Calgary to Amsterdam direct air service effective October 28, 1996.
It said the decision to halt the flights, which it currently operates three times a week, "was based mainly on the less than anticipated profitability of winter sales."

"KLM has been quite successful in the Calgary market, but the recent efforts to expand our services here with dedicated aircraft have not been up to expectations," said Ed Forsythe, Director of Marketing and Public Relations for KLM Canada.

Our goal has always been to increase the level of service out of Calgary but with declining fare levels particularly during the winter months, losses have exceeded summer profits with no improvement in sight," he said.

Together with KLM's global partner, Northwest Airlines, routings from Calgary via the Minneapolis hub connect with twice daily KLM/Northwest flights to Amsterdam. Beginning with the 1997 travel season, KLM plans to increase, from current levels, the total number of air seats from Canada to Amsterdam from its Vancouver, Montreal and Toronto gateways.
It said 12 KLM employees in Calgary would be affected by the flight cancellations, and alternative employment was being considered for a number of them.
KLM first began direct service between Amsterdam and Calgary more than 10 years ago, it said.
